reservation_menu.prompt: What would you like to do?

steps.text: To change a reservation, go to your confirmation text and click on the link. From there, select cancel reservation, after canceling you can make a new reservation or leave it cancelled.

steps.question: Are there any balls and/or white objects around the hitting area?
steps.subtext: If the simulator sees other balls, rubber tees or white objects it will not be able to identify your ball. The area it can see is much larger than the hitting mat.
steps.buttonText: There are no balls and/or white objects around the hitting area

steps.question: Have you reset the cameras?
steps.subtext: Click the IDRA button at the top of the screen, then select "Reset". Give it a few seconds to reconnect, then hit a test shot.

steps.question: Are your irons being picked up but your driver is not?
steps.subtext: If your irons read but your driver does not, switch to regular tees and place the tee closer to the middle of the hitting mat.
steps.buttonText: Switched to regular tees and moved closer to center

steps.question: Have you restarted the computer?
steps.subtext: The computer may need to be restarted. Press the Windows key, then click on the power button, then select restart.

steps.question: Is the ball centered in the strike zone?
steps.subtext: Re-center the ball exactly in the strike zone. Try a clean white ball and test again.

steps.text: Text (502) 410-2382 to create a maintenance ticket.

steps.question: Is the simulator turned on?
steps.subtext: Often the simulator is not turned on. You need to select a time on the white switch near the monitor.

steps.question: Have you reconnected the USB cables?
steps.subtext: On the front of the computer there are 2 black USB cables. Unplug them, wait 10 seconds, and plug them back in. Do NOT unplug anything on the back of the computer.

steps.question: Have you restarted the computer?
steps.subtext: If the cables have been reconnected and it still hasn't fixed it, restart the computer. Press the Windows key, then click on the power button, then select restart.

steps.text: Retry in the app. If it's still not working, text (502) 410-2382 to create a maintenance ticket.

steps.question: Have you reconnected the USB-C hub?

protee_menu.prompt: What are you having an issue with?

steps.question: Does it say "Connected" in the top right with a green circle?
steps.subtext: Check the top-right corner of ProTee Labs. If it doesn't say "Connected" with a green circle, click on the "not connected" circle, when the screen comes up, click on device → connect.

steps.question: Is it still not connecting?
steps.subtext: If that does not connect, walk to the screen with a golf club and look at the back of the simulator, locate the red switch, and turn it off, wait 10 seconds then turn it back on, so the red light is on.

steps.question: Have you restarted the computer?
steps.subtext: Go back to the computer, and restart the computer (Windows button, power icon, then select restart). When the computer restarts, select ProTee Labs.
steps.buttonText: Computer restarted and ProTee Labs opened

steps.question: Is the ball too far to the sides?
steps.subtext: The ball is too far to the sides, move the ball closer to the middle. You should have the tees setup close to the middle. The device can only pickup the ball 9" from the center on either side.

steps.question: Are there too many balls or white objects in view?
steps.subtext: There are too many balls within the simulator's view - move them further away. There are too many white objects within the simulator's view - move them away.
steps.buttonText: Balls and white objects moved away

steps.question: Have you tried restarting again?
steps.subtext: Restart the computer (Windows button, power icon, then select restart). When the computer restarts, select ProTee Labs. Test reads.

steps.text: Text (502) 410-2382 to create a maintenance ticket.

steps.question: How do I start a course on TGC 2019?
steps.subtext: Select Create Local Match, then select "Change Course". When you are looking at courses, you can select "More Filters" from there, you can type in any course name.

steps.text: Tip: look for the highest rated courses. Courses with "L" are typically the most similar to the actual course as they use lidar to create course.

skytrak_connect.prompt: What color is the middle light?

steps.question: Is the SkyTrak device off?
steps.subtext: Turn on the SkyTrak device. The power button is on the bottom left of the device. Make sure the computer is on the correct wifi network. Wifi Network Name: Bay[bay number]. The password is "BirdiePutt[bay number]"
steps.buttonText: SkyTrak turned on and on correct WiFi

steps.question: Is the app still not connecting?
steps.subtext: If you are on the correct wifi network, close out of the SkyTrak app (Windows key, then right click on the SkyTrak app at the bottom, then close, then click back on the SkyTrak app and click the button to close the app. Once, back on the desktop screen, reopen the SkyTrak app.

steps.question: Is the middle light yellow?
steps.subtext: Yellow means the SkyTrak is online but not linked to the app. Fully close the app (Windows key → right-click taskbar app → Close) → Reopen. Ensure PC is on bay Wi-Fi: Wifi Network Name: Bay[bay number], Password: BirdiePutt[bay number]
steps.buttonText: App closed and reopened, on correct WiFi

steps.question: Is the middle light solid green?
steps.subtext: Confirm PC is on bay Wi-Fi: Wifi Network Name: Bay[bay number], Password: BirdiePutt[bay number]. If still not connecting, connect PC to "skytrakplus" network

steps.question: Is the app still not connecting?
steps.subtext: App should connect; if not, fully close & reopen app. Switch to Network Mode → Setup SkyTrak Plus → Scan/select Wifi Network Name: Bay[bay number], Password: BirdiePutt[bay number]

steps.question: Has the SkyTrak light turned yellow?
steps.subtext: When the SkyTrak's middle light turns yellow, select the Windows key, then go to the wifi network. Connect the wifi to Wifi Network Name: Bay[bay number]. The password is "BirdiePutt[bay number]"

steps.question: Is the app still not connecting?
steps.subtext: If the app does not connect, click the Windows button, close the SkyTrak app, then re-open the SkyTrak app from the home screen. If that does not work and the SkyTrak middle light is still yellow, restart the PC (Windows button, click on the power icon and restart, then reopen the SkyTrak app.

steps.question: Is the middle light red?
steps.subtext: This is complicated and I recommend moving to another bay. If that is not possible, hit the Windows key, and click on the wifi networks in the bottom right. Connect to the Skytrak network that is showing. The password is "skytrakplus".

steps.question: Is the app connected now?
steps.subtext: Once the wifi is connected, the app should connect, if it doesn't, hit the Windows key, then right click on the SkyTrak app at the bottom, then close, then click back on the SkyTrak app and click the button to close the app. Once, back on the desktop screen, reopen the SkyTrak app.

steps.question: Have you switched to Network Mode?
steps.subtext: Once the device is connected, click where it says "Connected in Direct Mode", then select "Network Mode", select the setup for the "Skytrak Plus". Once in the Skytrak Plus setup, scan for networks and select Wifi Network Name: Bay[bay number]. The password is "BirdiePutt[bay number]". Click connect
steps.buttonText: Switched to Network Mode and connected

steps.question: Has the SkyTrak light turned yellow?
steps.subtext: When the SkyTrak's middle light turns yellow, select the Windows key, then go to the wifi network. Connect the wifi to Wifi Network Name: Bay[bay number]. The password is "BirdiePutt[bay number]"

steps.question: Is the app still not connecting?
steps.subtext: If the app does not connect, click the Windows button, close the SkyTrak app, then re-open the SkyTrak app from the home screen. If that does not work and the SkyTrak middle light is still yellow, restart the PC (Windows button, click on the power icon and restart, then reopen the SkyTrak app.

steps.question: Are you placing the ball on the red dot?
steps.subtext: Make sure you are placing the ball on the red dot. When hitting off a tee, put the red dot on the base of the tee. Feel free to move the SkyTrak.

steps.question: Is it still not picking up?
steps.subtext: If it is still not picking up, turn the SkyTrak off (button on the back of the SkyTrak), let it sit for 20 seconds, and then power it back on.

steps.question: Is this a left-handed bay?
steps.subtext: This mainly happens on the left-handed bay. Is the SkyTrak set to the correct hand-ness? Go to settings and check.

steps.question: Is the monitor on?
steps.subtext: Make sure the monitor is on. The power button is under the bottom right corner. Click the button on.

steps.question: Is the computer off or asleep?
steps.subtext: The computer is off. Make sure the computer is lit up, if it is not and you have tried to wake up the computer, click on the power button. Depending on the PC, it is either on the front of the PC or on the top.

steps.question: Is the computer not on?
steps.subtext: Make sure the computer is lit up, if it is not and you have tried to wake up the computer, click on the power button. Depending on the PC, it is either on the front of the PC or on the top.

steps.question: Is the projector on?
steps.subtext: Take the remote and point it at the projector. The projector is located behind the hitting area (the simulator is in front).

steps.question: Is the bay missing a remote?
steps.subtext: If the bay is missing a remote, find a remote from another similar bay (group or single) to turn it on.

steps.question: Is the aspect ratio off?
steps.subtext: The ratio on the single bays in Clarksville should be set to 4:3. Point the remote at the projector and click the "☰" button, select aspect ratio and then click 4:3. Then click the back button to get back to the game. (Only for single bays at Clarksville - do not change the aspect ratio on any other bays)
